anchors.implied_move_source: https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/delayed_quotes/options/ABM.json (Sep-18 45-strike straddle mid $3.95 / spot $47.05 = 8.4%; reconfirmed today, unchanged from stage 2's figure)

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: 8.4% implied is rich versus the 5.81% mean / 6.08% median absolute realised over the last six prints; I model ~5-7% realised with a downward skew. The straddle is over-priced for magnitude but the direction is not priced in -- at $47.05, one point off the $50.12 52-week high with all 8 covering analysts at Buy and a $52.43 mean target, a clean beat is already the base case embedded in the price.
key_drivers: The bar is a hockey stick. H1 FY26 adjusted EPS was $1.73 -- dead flat versus H1 FY25 $1.73 -- yet FY26 guidance of $3.85-$4.15 requires H2 of $2.12-$2.42 against H2 FY25 of $1.71, i.e. +24% to +42%. Q3 consensus of $1.04 on $2.32B is +26.8% EPS on +4% revenue against a Q3 FY25 base of $0.82 on $2,224.0M.

The metric that matters is segment operating margin, not EPS. Q3 FY25 segment operating profit was $170.4M on $2,224.0M = 7.66%. To print $1.04 with interest expense guided up to ~$110M FY26, ABM needs roughly 8.2%+ segment margin -- up ~55bp yoy and ~90bp sequentially from Q2 FY26's 7.3%. Two consecutive quarters have failed to deliver the inflection now required in one.

Mix is the offset and it is real: ATS/Technical Solutions +27.2% and Aviation +19.5% in Q2 on battery energy storage and data-center demand, M&D +16.5%, record H1 bookings of $1.2B. But B&I -- the largest segment -- was flat, so the margin recovery has to come entirely from ATS service-mix conversion landing on schedule.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The market is not currently paying ABM on margin. Last quarter the stock rose 6.67% on a print that grew revenue 8.4% but let segment margin fall 60bp -- it paid for ATS growth, record bookings and the data-center adjacency. A strong Q3 bookings figure and Q3's seasonally large free cash flow could carry the stock higher even if EPS lands at $0.95-1.00 and margin disappoints.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source quarter-specific 30/60/90-day estimate revision deltas; Q3 FY26 free-cash-flow consensus and the per-share size of the Q3 FY25 self-insurance adjustment are unavailable.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: The 8.4% anchor (Sep-18 45-strike straddle) sits on a strike $2.05 ITM with $5 spacing and total front-expiry OI of only 40 calls / 53 puts -- bid-side marks 6.9%, ask-side 9.9%. Strike-adjusted for moneyness and backed out against the Oct-16 base vol, my day-one event component is only ~4.8-5.5%. Against a realised mean abs of 5.81%, actual day-one implied is fair-to-slightly-cheap, not rich; working expectation +/-5-7% with a fat left tail.
key_drivers: Squeeze fuel is gone: short interest 3.2% of free float and down ~25% over the past month, borrow below 0.35%. Shorts covered INTO the print -- removes the covering bid that cushions a bad number, and leaves no fuel for an upside squeeze.
Options give no positioning edge: entire Sep-18 chain carries 40 call / 53 put OI, no pin, no gamma wall. Put/call 0.14 sits at its own 20-day average -- flow is neutral, not a signal.

Crowded-complacent consensus with no de-risking: 8 Buys, $52.43 mean target vs $47.05 spot, estimates unrevised for 30 days -- the exact configuration that produced the -8.67% and -9.07% gaps historically.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: ABM rarely misses revenue, and the most recent print gapped it +6.67%. A simple reaffirm-or-nudge-up at Q3 removes the guidance tail I am leaning on, and with no short base to sell into the rally, a relief gap of 6-8% is entirely available.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source IV rank/percentile, dealer gamma/GEX, or a current FINRA-dated short-interest settlement figure; short-interest figures are Ortex-derived and two days stale.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: 8.4% implied looks rich versus 5.81% mean / 6.08% median absolute over the last 6 prints; I expect a 5-7% absolute move with a downward skew. I would be a seller of the straddle, not a buyer of it.
key_drivers: There is effectively no retail crowd to read: StockTwits sentiment/message-volume fields return N/A. Any 'sentiment is bullish' claim here rests on media and positioning, not demand.

Positioning has quietly leaned long into the print: short interest 3.2% of float and down ~25% as shorts covered, put/call 0.14, MarketBeat news-sentiment score above the Industrials average. Bearish fuel removed, cushion gone.

Fragile narrative + fading momentum: the 'AI data-center infrastructure play' story is real (Technical Solutions +27% last quarter) but the stock is ~4% lower on the month, and last quarter revenue beat while EPS missed -- margins and cash conversion are the seam the story cannot absorb, and this print is the first proof point of the promised H2 ramp.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The sell side is Hold-heavy and the stock sits below a ~$52 consensus target -- the long side is not actually crowded in the institutional book. Another 25%+ Technical Solutions quarter plus a reaffirm gives the AI-adjacency bid everything it needs, and June's print delivered a +6.7% day that extended further.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source any quantified 7/14/30-day retail sentiment trend; the directional tilt rests on positioning, media tone counts, and one-month price drift, all snippet- or single-source-only.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Base-rate one-day move is ±5.8% mean abs / ±6.1% median abs over 6 sourced prints. The pure event component is nearer 7% once decomposed from the 11-DTE straddle. The distribution is left-skewed: 2 of 6 prints breached 8.4% and both were down.
key_drivers: Directional hit rate is a genuine coin-flip: 3 up / 3 down over 6 sourced prints (n=6). The tilt is in magnitude, not frequency -- mean down move 7.45% vs mean up move 4.16%.

Company-specific surprise base rate is the strongest signal: adjusted EPS missed consensus in roughly 5 of the last 7 quarters, with only Q2 FY26 a beat. Q3 FY26 consensus of $1.04 requires +26.8% YoY EPS growth against that record (n=7).

Run-up cohort is unfavourable: +13.6% over one month into the print, at roughly the 84th percentile of the 52-week range. Post-print drift has been negative in 2 of 3 follow-through windows sourced (n=3).
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The miss streak already broke in Q2 FY26 and the 90-day re-rating says the market is pricing a margin inflection. If Q3 delivers that inflection and guidance is reaffirmed or raised, the momentum/beat cohort base rate flips positive and this prints +5% to +8%.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Sample is 6 prints for magnitudes -- under my eight-observation threshold, hence Low confidence. Could not source reliable close-to-close percentages for pre-2025 quarters to extend it.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I model ~6-7% realised, below the 8.4% event-implied. There is no macro print on 2026-09-08 to widen the tail (CPI is 09-11, FOMC 09-16, Fed blackout began 09-05). Skew, not magnitude, is where the edge is.
key_drivers: Rates regime binds directly: Aug payrolls printed well above consensus, 2y yields hit their highest since Jan-2025, and Fed-hike odds rose. ABM carries floating-rate exposure and FY26 interest expense already guided up -- more than a tiebreaker for a small-cap-value, labour-heavy balance sheet in the cohort being sold.

Peer prints this season have been mixed-but-rewarding in services: Aramark beat and raised, traded +8.2%; Vestis missed badly yet popped ~8% on an FCF guidance raise; the tape is paying for cash flow and forward narrative, largely forgiving the printed quarter.

Two directly opposed segment read-throughs: bearish jet-fuel-cost pressure on ABM Aviation from airline capacity cuts; bullish CBRE/EMCOR/Comfort Systems data-centre and electrical demand confirming the backdrop ABM's Technical Solutions and WGNSTAR deal sit against.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The single strongest risk is that ABM leans the call into the AI/data-centre narrative in a tape where XLI's YTD gain is being driven almost entirely by data-centre capex, and gets paid a re-rating regardless of the printed margin -- Vestis proved this season that a large headline miss can still trade +8% on the forward story.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source ABM short interest or ETF/index flow figures specific to ABM; 2y-yield levels are snippet_only from secondary reporting.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I expect a realised one-day move of roughly 5-7%, slightly below the 8.4% implied, which likely overstates the true event premium since the reference strike is ~2 points in-the-money with 10 days of post-event life.
panel_verdicts.consensus_view_as_i_read_it: Mildly bullish. Record Q2 revenue, +6.67% reaction; H1 bookings a company-record $1.2bn; Technical Solutions and M&D growing on semiconductor/data-centre demand; 8 analysts Buy at an 11.4x forward P/E. The plain read is: cheap self-help name with an AI-adjacent growth engine beats and re-rates.
panel_verdicts.strongest_reversal_case: Consensus wants +26.8% EPS growth on +4% revenue -- a margin-inflection bar after two consecutive quarters of margin contraction and two consecutive EPS misses. The FY guide is fully back-half loaded (H1 FY26 flat YoY). No squeeze fuel and no washout: short interest falling, borrow low, insider activity is net selling. The exact precedent: last year's Q3 (5 Sep 2025) missed and guided to the low end.
panel_verdicts.what_would_break_my_reversal_case: A Q3 print at or above $1.04 with segment operating margin up year over year, plus a narrowing of FY26 guidance into the upper half and a third straight quarter of positive FCF -- at 11.4x forward that validates the H2 ramp and the stock re-rates up hard.
key_drivers: Consensus wants +26.8% EPS growth on +4% revenue -- a margin-inflection bar after two consecutive quarters of contraction
FY guide is fully back-half loaded: H1 FY26 adj. EPS $1.73 vs H1 FY25 $1.73
No squeeze fuel and no washout: short interest 3.2% of float and falling, borrow <0.35%, insider activity net selling
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: ABM's investor base is demonstrably trading this on revenue, bookings and cash conversion rather than EPS precision -- Q2 was an EPS miss and the stock still rose 6.67%. A record-bookings, FCF-improving quarter with a reaffirmed guide could be rewarded again.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Q3 FY26 consensus conflicts by source ($0.91 vs $1.04); used $1.04 because it reconciles with the sourced +26.8% YoY figure. Could not source current-quarter segment-level consensus or the buy-side whisper.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I expect ~5.5-6.5% absolute, below the 8.4% straddle-implied. Event vol looks full-to-rich, and the skew of my forensic read is mildly to the downside within that range.
panel_verdicts.insider_signal: Routine 10b5-1 / tax-withholding selling -- no informative cluster. Zero insider purchases in 2025 or 2026, which is ABM's baseline, not a new signal. One small discretionary CAO sale (~$179k) is weak. No Form 4, Form 144 or 8-K of any kind since 2026-07-17 -- a clean seven-week run-in with no cadence anomaly and no pre-announcement.
panel_verdicts.communication_signal: A deferral, not a downgrade. ABM reaffirmed FY26 adjusted EPS of $3.85-$4.15 for the second consecutive quarter while upgrading only the revenue qualifier, and explicitly pushed profitability into the future on the Q2 call ('you'll see the margins ramp in the back half'). Meanwhile B&I revenue was flat with operating margin down YoY, with named client exits carrying into Q3-Q4. H1 adjusted EPS of $1.73 leaves a steep back-loaded ramp whose first checkpoint is this print.
key_drivers: Back-half margin ramp explicitly promised on the Q2 call is being tested for the first time, against a declining-margin B&I segment with named client exits
Insider tape is genuinely empty of information: everything scheduled or tax-related, no buying, no filings at all since 2026-07-17
Positioning is light and unopinionated -- short interest falling, borrow low, put/call near its 20-day average -- no squeeze fuel and no informed-flow tell either way
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: My lean rests almost entirely on language, and the same setup resolved upward last quarter (+6.67%). Positioning is clean, shorts have already covered, estimates have been flat for two months, and an ATS/Aviation-led beat could deliver a narrowed guide into the upper half -- with nobody positioned short, that print is bought hard and my forensic read is simply irrelevant to the outcome.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source Glassdoor rating drift, dark-pool prints, or any specific unusual options block; short-interest, borrow and put/call figures are snippet_only from a 2026-09-05 Ortex piece, not the exchange tape.

synthesis.move_band_note: unsigned magnitude band, right-skewed; the implied move is roughly one standard deviation, not a cap
synthesis.chair_override_note: certainty_tier overridden High -> Med. Four of seven personas (options-positioning, sentiment, red-team, forensics) leaned in part on the same single source (ortex.news, 'ABM Industries: ERP Scars Meet a Critical Print') for a shared 'shorts already covered, no squeeze fuel' framing element of their bearish case. The panel's unusually tight disparity (6.6, the tightest read of either panelled name) is partly an artifact of that shared input rather than seven fully independent reads converging on their own -- exactly the case synthesis-chair.md flags for a certainty markdown, not a call or move override.
synthesis.early_prediction: Panel leans mildly bearish and unusually tightly so (consensus -16.7, disparity 6.6) -- all seven personas cluster in the -12 to -20 range on a stretched back-half FY26 margin bridge against an 8.4% implied move that is rich versus the 5.81% historical mean. Independence is imperfect (see chair_override_note), so certainty is held to Med despite the mechanical High score. Main caveat: red-team reversal risk hits 65/100 on a specific, well-sourced case, and three of ABM's last four EPS misses have still produced flat-to-up sessions.
synthesis.red_team_survival_note: The red-team case (-20, reversal_risk 65) is specific and sourced. No dissenting persona answers it directly -- all seven land bearish -- but every persona who scored it also independently flagged the same counter-risk: the market has repeatedly paid ABM for revenue, bookings and AI-adjacency growth even on EPS or margin misses. The thesis survives contact with the reversal case only provisionally.

independence_note: Seven isolated subagents; each received only the Phase-0 anchors (ticker, company, window, session, spot, implied move, historical realised moves) -- no dossier, no preliminary direction score, no other persona's verdict.
